simple.meaning: דּוּשׁ (dûwsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to trample or thresh.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 14 times across Deuteronomy, Judges, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, Job, and 5 more, beginning at Deuteronomy 25:4. Its contexts include family line, kingship, mountain, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוּשׁ (H1758).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דּוּשׁ (dûwsh) / H1758 is traced through Deuteronomy 25:4, Judges 8:7, 2 Kings 13:7, 1 Chronicles 21:20 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: break, tear, thresh, tread out (down), at grass (Jeremiah 50:11, by mistake for 1877 ).
